rationale: Much of the partition follows substantive scientific questions, but several families combine distinct problems using generic evaluation language or broad conceptual labels. The grouping also separates closely equivalent adversarial-robustness questions without a clear substantive distinction. These concerns exceed isolated debatable placements and prevent the partition from consistently functioning as a grouping into distinct scientific problem families.

observations.family: Demarcation and measurement of latent agent properties
observations.assessment: This family combines the boundary between computational and physical effects, independence of information and action, and the influence of latent competencies on decisions. These concern different constructs and relationships. Their shared emphasis on measurement does not establish a substantive common problem, and Q022 does not specifically address a latent agent property.

observations.family: Comparative benchmarking of simulation and learning implementations
observations.assessment: Q041, Q042, and Q064 share a meaningful scalability concern. However, Q026 centers on uncertainty propagation and Q028 on multimodal learning. The family appears to rely substantially on their common repository-oriented evaluation format, which groups different scientific problems under a generic benchmarking label.

observations.family: Adversarial attacks on learned world models; Safety evaluation frameworks, metrics and interpretability
observations.assessment: Q053 asks how to evaluate robustness to adversarial attacks across threat contexts, while Q056 asks how to evaluate robustness across threat landscapes and identify security factors. Q023 and Q034 also concern robustness evaluation. Assigning Q056 to evaluation while the others are assigned to attacks splits substantially the same problem without an evident scientific boundary.

Q021, Q036, Q039, and Q072 form a defensible core around the behavior and reliability of systems that modify themselves. Q012 explicitly connects self-modification to cooperation. Q007 instead asks about memory and complex behavior, and Q002 about external trace ecology and world-model development; neither establishes the self-modification or stability relationship needed to connect it clearly to the core. This is a material breadth ambiguity.

Q001, Q013, Q027, and Q055 have a plausible shared focus on consciousness, experience, and global availability. Q015 concerns distinguishing architecture from identity, and Q075 concerns identity scale. Their inclusion is conceivable within a broad conceptual program, but the supplied text does not establish a common scientific question connecting identity measurement to consciousness.

observations.family: Predictive safety shields versus safety illusions
observations.assessment: This is a coherent substantive family: its questions concern when predictive models provide reliable safety protection and when reliance on them produces misleading safety assurances. Over-trust and safe-versus-unsafe trajectory discrimination fit that shared problem.

The family consistently addresses robustness, prediction, or evaluation during adaptation to changing environments. Q051 does not explicitly require a long horizon, but its emphasis on unexpected environmental changes and adaptation makes the placement defensible.

observations.family: State grounding and imagination fidelity; Representation choice and cross-environment generalization
observations.assessment: These families have a defensible distinction between connecting observations to useful environmental states and transferring representations or generated scenarios across tasks and environments. Q050 overlaps with representation choice, and Q068 overlaps with imagination, but these individual ambiguities do not independently invalidate the grouping.
